ety.text: lie (“to rest in a horizontal position”) + -ing.

senses.d: The act of one who lies, or keeps low to the ground.
ex:
1854, Saint Augustine, Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm LXIV, translated by Philip Schaff et al.
But whom could the lyings in wait of the human heart escape?

senses.d: An act or telling a lie or falsehood; the practice of telling lies.
Tending to tell lies, untruthful, mendacious
ex: Gloster: Then, Saunder, sit there, the lyingest knave in Christendom.

grp.label: act of keeping low to the ground

es:decúbito.gl: position (of the body when lying down)

ety.text: Borrowed from New Latin dēcubitus (“lying down”).
